<thought>Both the ¹H NMR (a single aromatic signal integrating to 10 H) and the ¹³C NMR (a carbonyl carbon at ~196 ppm plus aromatic carbons) point to a symmetric diaryl ketone. The molecular weight expected for C₁₃H₁₀O (benzophenone) is 182 Da, which matches the typical mass spectrum of such a compound. Therefore the most plausible structure is benzophenone, whose SMILES string is “O(C1=CC=CC=C1)C2=CC=CC=C2”.</thought>
<final_answer>O(C1=CC=CC=C1)C2=CC=CC=C2</final_answer>
